_purpose: Reference scenarios for evaluating keyboard-trap detection (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap). Expected verdicts are specified from the success criterion, independently of any detector implementation. Detectors must never read this file. Do not edit an expected verdict to make a detector pass; if a verdict is wrong, change it in a separate, reviewed commit with the reason, and update EXPECTED_SHA256.
_criterion: 2.1.2: If keyboard focus can be moved to a component using a keyboard interface, focus can be moved away from that component using only a keyboard interface; if more than unmodified arrow or tab keys or other standard exit methods are required, the user is advised of the method. Standard exit methods include Tab, Shift+Tab and Escape.
_verdicts: VIOLATION = focus cannot be moved away with Tab, Shift+Tab or Escape. NOT_A_VIOLATION = focus can be moved away (including legitimate containment such as a modal dialog that Escape closes). INCONCLUSIVE = the outcome cannot be observed from the page (e.g. focus inside a cross-origin frame that never returns).

cases.rationale: Tab visits three links and then leaves the document for the browser; this is ordinary cycling.
Focus keeps moving to new links; a page longer than the Tab budget is not a trap.
Twelve distinct buttons share an identical long class attribute; focus moves between distinct elements.
Three adjacent links with identical markup and text ('Read more') are three separate focus stops, not one stuck element.

cases.rationale: Once focused, the field swallows Tab, Shift+Tab and Escape; focus cannot leave by keyboard and no method is advised.
A three-button widget wraps Tab and Shift+Tab inside itself and ignores Escape; other controls on the page are unreachable afterwards.
An open modal keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside itself, which is legitimate containment, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the page.

cases.rationale: A native <dialog> opened with showModal() can be closed with Escape; focus can leave it.
A closed disclosure menu is one Tab stop; Tab continues past it.

cases.rationale: Focus enters a cross-origin frame and returns to the page by Tab; the frame's internals are not visible, but focus demonstrably left it.

cases.rationale: Focus enters a cross-origin frame whose content swallows Tab; from the parent page it is impossible to observe whether focus is trapped or still moving inside the frame, or whether another exit exists.
Each time the last button is focused a new button is added after it; focus keeps moving to new, distinct controls.
With one link, Tab alternates between the link and the browser; the same element repeating is normal cycling.
Nothing can receive focus, so nothing can trap it.
A widget wraps Tab forward inside itself but Shift+Tab is not intercepted, so focus can leave with a standard key.
An editor keeps Tab (to insert indentation) but Escape releases it, after which Tab moves on; Escape is a standard exit method.
